beats.fact: OAPEC declares an oil embargo against the US and other backers of Israel after the Yom Kippur War; crude prices quadruple from about $3 to $12 per barrel
Dow falls below 900 as the embargo bites; US inflation runs above 10% and the 1973-75 recession deepens
Nixon resigns over Watergate (Aug 8), accelerating the slide; the Dow drops from about 800 toward 650 within a month
Dow bottoms at 577.60 (Dec 6), down 45% from its January 1973 peak; UK stocks fall even further
Iranian revolution halts oil exports; the second oil shock roughly doubles crude prices and US inflation surges past 11%
Volcker's 'Saturday night special' (Oct 6): the Fed lifts its discount rate to 12% and shifts to money-supply targeting, letting rates spike toward 20%
Silver Thursday (Mar 27): the Hunt brothers miss margin calls as silver collapses, panicking commodity markets; gold had hit a record $850 on Jan 21
Mexico suspends debt payments (Aug 12), igniting the Latin American debt crisis; the same week the Dow bottoms at 776.91 before a new bull market
Black Monday (Oct 19): the Dow plunges 22.6% in one day, still the worst ever, with an estimated $1.7 trillion of global equity value erased
Hong Kong's exchange shuts for four days; on reopening (Oct 26) the Hang Seng crashes 33%
Dow rebounds a record 10.2% on Oct 21 as the Fed under Greenspan pledges liquidity support
Reagan names the Brady Commission (Oct 27) to investigate; its report leads to market-wide circuit breakers in 1988
Nikkei 225 closes at its all-time high of 38,915.87 (Dec 29) at the top of the Heisei bubble, with record Tokyo land prices
New-year selling kicks off the slide; Japan curbs real-estate lending and the Nikkei ends 1990 down 39%
Iraq invades Kuwait (Aug 2), doubling oil prices and deepening the world bear market; the Bank of Japan lifts its discount rate to 6% (Aug 30)
Nikkei bottoms near 14,309, down 63% from the peak; bad loans cascade into the 'lost decade' - the index only bottoms near 7,600 in 2003
Thailand floats the baht (Jul 2); it loses about 20% at once and contagion hits the Philippines, Malaysia and Indonesia
Hang Seng drops 23% in four days (Oct 20-23); the Dow falls 554 points (Oct 27), triggering its first-ever circuit-breaker halt
Korea signs a record $58bn IMF rescue (Dec 3) as its reserves nearly run dry; major chaebol collapse
Indonesia's rupiah crumbles from about 2,400 to roughly 16,000 per dollar; food riots follow and Suharto resigns in May 1998
Russia devalues the ruble, defaults on domestic GKO debt and declares a 90-day foreign-debt moratorium (Aug 17); the ruble loses most of its value within weeks
The New York Fed brokers a $3.6bn private rescue of hedge fund LTCM (Sep 23) after its leveraged convergence trades implode
The Fed cuts rates (Sep 29) but equities keep sliding; the S&P 500 bottoms Oct 8 about 19% below its July peak
Surprise inter-meeting Fed cut (Oct 15) sparks a powerful rally; Brazil's real devaluation in Jan 1999 caps the EM panic
Nasdaq peaks at 5,048.62 (Mar 10) after a five-year 600% run; dot-com IPO valuations reach absurd extremes
Nasdaq plunges 25% in one week (Apr 10-14) as the Microsoft antitrust ruling and vanishing earnings burst the mania
Enron files for bankruptcy (Dec 2), then the largest in US history, after accounting fraud; WorldCom follows with an even bigger filing in Jul 2002
Nasdaq bottoms at 1,114.11 (Oct 9), down 78% from its peak and wiping out roughly $5 trillion of market value
BNP Paribas freezes three funds (Aug 9) as subprime valuations evaporate; interbank lending seizes up
Bear Stearns nears collapse and is sold to JPMorgan in a Fed-backed fire sale (Mar 16)
Lehman files the largest bankruptcy in US history (Sep 15); AIG is rescued the next day; the House rejects TARP (Sep 29) and the Dow falls 777 points
S&P 500 bottoms at 676.53 (Mar 9), down 57% from its Oct 2007 peak; the Fed ramps up QE and a new bull market begins
Greece's new government reveals a budget deficit far larger than reported (revised toward 13% of GDP); rating downgrades follow
First Greek bailout: eurozone and IMF agree EUR 110bn (May 2); the EFSF is created; the May 6 'flash crash' hits US markets
Italian 10-year yields top 7%; Berlusconi resigns (Nov 12) as technocratic governments take over in Rome and Athens
Draghi pledges to do 'whatever it takes' (Jul 26) after Greece's record sovereign debt restructuring (Mar); the OMT programme announced in Sep caps the crisis

crises.name: EM Selloff & Fed Tightening (Turkish Lira Crisis)

beats.fact: US sanctions on Rusal sink the ruble; Argentina's peso collapse forces 40% interest rates and a $50bn IMF standby in June
Trump doubles metals tariffs on Turkey (Aug 10); the lira plunges about 25% in days toward 7.2/USD, rattling European banks
Fed's third hike of the year (Sep 26) plus 3.2% 10-year Treasury yields; the MSCI EM index is down roughly 25% from its January peak
Fourth Fed hike; the S&P 500 falls 9.2% in December, worst since 1931, bottoming Dec 24 nearly 20% below its September peak
COVID-19 supply shock ends the longest US bull market; the S&P 500 peaks Feb 19 and suffers its fastest-ever 10% correction
OPEC+ talks collapse (Mar 6) and Saudi Arabia starts a price war; oil crashes about 25% on Mar 9, tripping the first of four circuit breakers
Fed cuts to zero and launches $700bn QE (Mar 15); S&P bottoms at 2,237.40 (Mar 23), down 33.9% in 23 sessions; the $2.2tn CARES Act follows (Mar 27)
S&P 500 reclaims its February record (Aug 18) after about 126 trading days - the shortest bear market on record
Russia invades Ukraine (Feb 24); Brent spikes past $120 and global inflation jumps again
The Fed begins its fastest hiking cycle since the 1980s (Mar 16), later adding 75bp moves; US CPI peaks at 9.1% in June
UK 'mini-budget' (Sep 23) triggers a gilt meltdown and LDI pension fire sales; sterling hits a record low and the Bank of England emergency-buys gilts (Sep 28)
S&P 500 bottoms at 3,577.03 (Oct 12), down 25.4%; the Nasdaq is off more than 35% and global bonds suffer their worst year in decades
